proposals.before: Formerly wuzi Xu's persuasion was listened to by He Lu, and the Wu king went far to Ying;
proposals.after: Formerly Wu Zixu's counsel was heeded by Helü, and the king of Wu pushed as far as Ying;
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English misspells 伍子胥 as 'wuzi Xu' and 闔閭 as 'He Lu'; use standard Wu Zixu and Helü.

proposals.before: Gao Di enfeoffed him as Yue Qing, numbered as Hua Cheng Jun.
proposals.after: Gao Di enfeoffed him at Yueqing and titled him Lord Huacheng.
proposals.reason: 號曰 means 'titled/called', not 'numbered'; 樂卿 is the fief place, not a personal name 'Yue Qing'.

proposals.before: Yue Yi thus served as envoy from Wei Zhao Wang to Yan, the Yan king treated him with guest courtesy.
proposals.after: Yue Yi thus served as envoy from King Zhao of Wei to Yan; the king of Yan treated him with guest courtesy.
proposals.reason: 'Wei Zhao Wang' is untranslated romanization; render as King Zhao of Wei for consistency with other royal titles.

decisions.reason: Focus unit names 伍子胥 and 闔閭; idiomatic 'wuzi Xu' and 'He Lu' are wrong name forms, while Wu Zixu and Helü restore the standard readings, and 遠跡至郢 is fairly rendered as pushing as far as Ying.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔伍子胥說聽於闔閭，而吳王遠跡至郢

decisions.reason: 封之樂卿 enfeoffs Yue Shu at the place 樂卿, and 號曰華成君 titles him Lord Huacheng; the before wrongly treats 樂卿 as a personal name and mistranslates 號曰 as 'numbered'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高帝封之樂卿，號曰華成君

decisions.reason: 魏昭王 is King Zhao of Wei; leaving 'Wei Zhao Wang' untranslated is a real title error, and the after matches the chapter's 'King Zhao of Yan' pattern while preserving 使於燕 and guest courtesy.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 樂毅於是為魏昭王使於燕

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English He Lu came only from the bad idiomatic of 闔閭; the personal-name claim must read Helü while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.

Accepted r0003 shows English Wei Zhao Wang came only from untranslated romanization of 魏昭王; the title claim must read King Zhao of Wei while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
